For root cause: the upstream payment provider began returning 503s for card lookups at 16:06, and io-shop's account page has no fallback or timeout guard around that call, so every account request failed — the underlying provider failure itself is outside my visibility.

For the executive summary, I'll note account pages became unavailable starting 16:06 UTC and were still failing at the end of the metrics window, caused by the third-party payment provider; the automated responder investigated, ruled out deploys/config/flag changes, found no safe automated remedy, and escalated with a draft PR for human review.

input.executive_summary:
Starting at 16:06 UTC on 25 September 2026, the account page of the online shop stopped working for shoppers. The page pulls saved card details from an outside payment company, and that company's service began rejecting those requests; because the page cannot render without them, essentially every attempt to open it failed instead of loading. Anyone trying to view their account during this window was affected; other parts of the shop that do not need payment details were not implicated. The service had not recovered by the time the last metrics were read, so the true length of the outage is not known from this record - it lasted at least from onset until the end of the available data.

The automated on-call system picked up the alert about six minutes after onset, pulled metrics, logs and change history, and correctly identified an outside supplier as the cause within roughly a minute, confirming there had been no recent software release or setting change on our side. Because the fault lay in someone else's system, the automation had no safe action of its own to take - it repeated its investigation three times, each time declining to act - and instead handed the incident to engineers, opening a draft code change for review that would let the account page survive the supplier being unavailable. No automated remediation was applied and nothing was rolled back. Recovery therefore depended on the supplier, and follow-up should cover contacting them and shipping the change so the page degrades gracefully rather than failing completely next time.
input.root_cause: The third-party payment provider io-shop depends on (api.io-pay.example) began returning HTTP 503 for card lookups (/v1/shoppers/{id}/card) at 16:06 UTC, and io-shop's account-page render path calls that endpoint with no fallback or degraded mode, so every account-page request that touched payment data failed outright (PaymentProviderFailed at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95). Nothing internal to io-shop changed: no deploy, release, config or feature-flag change was recorded in the windows checked, so the failure originated entirely upstream; why the provider itself started serving 503s is not visible from io-shop's telemetry.
